answer_text:
Let

\[
N=\binom n5=\frac{n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)(n-4)}{120}.
\]

Since \(N=\overline{ababab}\) is a six-digit repeating two-digit block, we may write

\[
N=(10a+b)(10000+100+1)=10101(10a+b).
\]

Also,

\[
10101=3\cdot 7\cdot 13\cdot 37.
\]

So \(N\) must be divisible by \(7,13,\) and \(37\).

Because \(a\neq 0\), we have

\[
101010\le N\le 999999.
\]

Using monotonicity of \(\binom n5\),

\[
\binom{28}{5}=98280,\qquad \binom{29}{5}=118755,
\]

and

\[
\binom{43}{5}=962598,\qquad \binom{44}{5}=1086008.
\]

Thus

\[
29\le n\le 43.
\]

Now use divisibility by \(37\). Since \(37\nmid 120\), we need

\[
37\mid n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)(n-4).
\]

In the range \(29\le n\le 43\), the only multiple of \(37\) that can appear among the five consecutive factors is \(37\) itself. Hence

\[
n\in\{37,38,39,40,41\}.
\]

Next use divisibility by \(7\). The five consecutive factors must contain a multiple of \(7\):

- \(n=37\): factors \(33,34,35,36,37\) contain \(35\).
- \(n=38\): factors \(34,35,36,37,38\) contain \(35\).
- \(n=39\): factors \(35,36,37,38,39\) contain \(35\).
- \(n=40\): factors \(36,37,38,39,40\) contain no multiple of \(7\).
- \(n=41\): factors \(37,38,39,40,41\) contain no multiple of \(7\).

So \(n\in\{37,38,39\}\).

Finally use divisibility by \(13\). The five consecutive factors must contain a multiple of \(13\):

- \(n=37\): factors \(33,34,35,36,37\) contain no multiple of \(13\).
- \(n=38\): factors \(34,35,36,37,38\) contain no multiple of \(13\).
- \(n=39\): factors \(35,36,37,38,39\) contain \(39=3\cdot 13\).

Thus the only possible value is

\[
n=39.
\]

Check:

\[
\binom{39}{5}=575757=\overline{575757}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\boxed{39}
\]
